stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) risk, which cytomegalovirus (CMV) factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: CMV serostatus has no relationship to PTLD risk
Only donor age determines CMV-related PTLD risk
CMV disease prevents PTLD from ever occurring

explanation.rationale_correct: Risk factors for PTLD include CMV disease and CMV mismatch with a CMV-seropositive donor and CMV-seronegative recipient, along with Epstein-Barr virus factors and potent immunosuppression.

rationale_incorrect.B: CMV disease and mismatch are listed among PTLD risk factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: CMV disease and serostatus patterns are key viral risk factors rather than donor age alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: CMV disease increases rather than eliminates PTLD risk.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → Epstein-Barr virus → 3. Risk factors for PTLD

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Epstein-Barr virus → 3.e. (CMV disease as PTLD risk factor); PDF p. 198 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. CMV-disease PTLD risk angle distinct from CMV D+/R− mismatch (cctc-2115) and EBV D+/R− recall (cctc-2109); anchor verified on Cupples p. 198.

stem: During pretransplant teaching about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) management, which therapy aligns with standard references?

options.text: Immediate intensification of all immunosuppression without evaluation
Rituximab is contraindicated in every PTLD case
PTLD is treated only with routine daily skin biopsy

explanation.rationale_correct: Treatment options for PTLD include reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression, mTOR inhibitors, rituximab, IVIG, antiviral therapy, surgery for localized disease, and cytotoxic chemotherapy such as R-CHOP.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression is reduced or modified rather than intensified as initial PTLD management.
rationale_incorrect.C: Rituximab is a listed treatment option rather than being universally contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.D: Targeted therapies such as rituximab are used rather than biopsy alone.

stem: When explaining advanced posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) treatment options, which cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen aligns with standard references?

options.text: R-CHOP with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone
No chemotherapy is ever used for PTLD
Routine daily oral aspirin as the sole cytotoxic regimen
Chemotherapy is limited to pretransplant candidates only

explanation.rationale_correct: Cytotoxic chemotherapy options for PTLD include R-CHOP with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone, along with other listed therapies.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cytotoxic chemotherapy is among advanced PTLD treatment options.
rationale_incorrect.C: R-CHOP is the referenced regimen rather than aspirin alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Chemotherapy may be used post-transplant for PTLD rather than being limited to pretransplant evaluation.

stem: A coordinator explains posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) treatment to a lung transplant candidate. Which option aligns with standard references for localized disease?

options.text: No surgical option exists for any PTLD presentation
Routine daily bone marrow biopsy as the only localized treatment
Surgery is contraindicated in every transplant recipient with PTLD

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD treatment options include surgery for localized disease, along with immunosuppression reduction, rituximab, IVIG, antiviral therapy, and chemotherapy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Surgery is listed for localized PTLD disease.
rationale_incorrect.C: Surgical resection is a treatment option rather than routine biopsy alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Surgery may be used for localized disease when indicated rather than being universally contraindicated.
